subject: MSA redline: liability caps, prohibited testing, and remedies
messages:
From: J. Harris <jharris@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: legal+contracts@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redline: prohibited testing + remedies

Rishi —

Thanks for sending the MSA draft. A couple of items that jumped out from our side that will need careful negotiation before procurement can sign:

1) Prohibited testing / benchmarking: the current draft broadly prohibits testing that impacts production or attempts to reverse engineer the model. We need to be able to conduct benchmark runs during POC and periodic performance checks. Can you confirm whether we can get a narrow benchmarking carve-out (e.g., non-production endpoints, rate limits, no scraping of training data)?

2) Remedies and injunctive relief: our legal team is pushing for unlimited injunctive relief to stop IP misuse and data exfiltration, but our procurement team is concerned about uncapped exposure. We are open to a carve-out for IP/confidentiality but want clarity on what Redwood considers an appropriate cap for other damages.

3) Liability cap math: the cap tied to 12 months of fees works for us in principle, but need to understand whether fees include professional services / onboarding credits and whether the cap floats from the Order Form start date or effective date.

Please loop in your legal team with redline suggestions so we can converge quickly. We’re targeting PO issuance by mid-June.

-JH
Partner Counsel, Acme Corp

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: MSA redline: prohibited testing + remedies

Team — forwarding Acme's note. They want: (a) a constrained benchmarking carve-out, (b) clarity on injunctive relief carveouts, and (c) how we calculate the monetary cap. Can legal propose fallback language we can send back by EOD tomorrow?

My thoughts: keep a strong confidentiality/IP injunctive carve-out uncapped, cap everything else to the greater of 12 months of paid fees or $5M, and allow limited benchmarking under an executed NDA and with explicit rate and data-use limits. Thoughts?

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: prohibited testing + remedies

Rishi / Laura —

High-level legal view and proposed redlines below. Aim is to minimize uncapped exposure while giving the customer the limited rights they need for procurement/ops testing.

Summary proposal (we can send as tracked changes):
- Monetary cap: "Company's aggregate liability for damages arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid to Redwood under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (b) USD 5,000,000."
- Carveouts (uncapped): IP infringement (third-party claims for Redwood IP), obligations to injunctive relief for breach of Confidential Information, and claims for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or intentional data exfiltration.
- Prohibited testing / benchmarking exception: allow benchmarking only if (i) conducted against a non-production/dedicated test tenant or sandbox, (ii) performed under an executed NDA and acceptable use annex, (iii) subject to rate limits and no attempts to extract training data or model weights, and (iv) results may be used for internal evaluation only (no public distribution). Include a procedure for requesting temporary production-like load testing with advance notice and Redwood approval.
- Fees included in cap: fees paid under the applicable Order Form for subscription and usage charges; exclude professional services only if explicitly invoiced as a one-time professional services line and the parties agree in the Order Form.

Sample clause language (for redline):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, neither party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, except that nothing in this Section shall limit: (a) either party's indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims; (b) remedies for breach of Confidential Information or misappropriation of Confidential Information; or (c) remedies that are not reasonably foreseeable. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the parties agree that injunctive relief shall be available to prevent or curtail a breach of this Agreement that threatens either party's intellectual property rights or Confidential Information. Monetary damages (other than the categories listed in (a)-(c)) shall be subject to the monetary cap set forth above."

Operational note: we should ask Acme to provide SOC2 summary and confirm the tenant/sandbox they plan to use for benchmarking. Also prepare a short "benchmarking rules" PDF we can attach to the Order Form (rate caps, test windows, contact info, sample query limits).

I can produce a tracked-redline MSA and a short benchmarking annex for Rishi to share.

-karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: prohibited testing + remedies

Agree with Karthik's approach. A few clarifications / escalation items: 

- I recommend preserving explicit injunctive relief for Confidential Information and IP (we don't negotiate that away). For all other categories (performance, lost profits), keep damages capped. 
- For benchmarking, add a clause: "Benchmarking permitted only after execution of the Benchmarking Annex and a supporting NDA; benchmarking shall not include attempts to reconstruct model weights, training data, or to circumvent rate limits." That gives us a standalone doc to evolve without reopening the MSA.
- If Acme insists on broader benchmarking or uncapped remedies beyond IP/confidentiality, route to Markus for commercial approval (likely needs CRO signoff).

I will review Karthik's tracked redline and aim to return the first pass by COB today.

-Laura
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: J. Harris <jharris@acme-corp.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: MSA redline: prohibited testing + remedies

JH / Samantha —

Thanks for the quick flag. Our legal team proposes a compromise that should address Acme's operational needs without exposing either side to open-ended risk. Key points we plan to send as redline: 

- Limited benchmarking carve-out (sandbox/non-prod only, executed NDA, explicit rate limits, results for internal use). See attached "benchmarking_rules.pdf" for suggested limits.
- Injunctive relief preserved for IP and Confidential Info only; monetary damages for other categories capped at the greater of 12 months' fees or $5M.
- Clarification that the 12-month lookback is measured from the Order Form start date and includes subscription and usage fees; professional services are excluded unless separately invoiced on the Order Form.

Attaching our tracked-redline MSA and the benchmarking rules for your review. If that looks broadly acceptable, Laura/karthik will finalize redlines and we can get procurement/PO moving. Targeting execution week of June 15 if we can close terms this week.

Subject: Re: MSA redline: liability / benchmarking compromise

Rishi / Laura —

Appreciate the proposed compromise. A few follow-ups before we can sign:

- Benchmarking: Acme will accept the sandbox approach provided Redwood confirms (a) the sandbox environment will be isolated from Acme production systems, and (b) Redwood will provide test-level rate limits and monitoring during the test window. Please confirm.
- Injunctive relief: Acme confirms the carve-out for IP / Confidential Information only. We would like the redline to explicitly reference trade secrets as a subset of Confidential Information.
- Cap math: please confirm whether "12 months' fees" includes usage overage charges; if so, we accept. Also please attach a short worksheet showing example cap calculations using our projected annual spend (we will send forecasts to you separately).
- Pre-reqs: before benchmarking starts we need an executed NDA (we will share ours if Redwood prefers) and a SOC 2 summary.

If you can send updated tracked changes and the benchmarking annex, we can circulate internally and push PO.

-JH
Partner Counsel, Acme Corp

Attachments: proposed_redline_MSA_Redwood.docx (redline), benchmarking_rules.pdf (annex draft), SOC2-summary.pdf (Redwood SOC 2 summary)
